front.title: Effect Acknowledgement for HTTP and Web Linking

abstract.t: This document specifies an Experimental HTTP binding for the QIK-VRT Effect Acknowledgement protocol. Structured Fields and Web Linking support capability discovery, preparation, independent validation of a responsibility record, and an exact-bound commit. A separately negotiated readback profile binds authoritative observations to the authorized action.

Transport receipt, authorization, execution and confirmation are separate facts. EFFECT_ACK_DONE retains its core meaning: eligibility for ordinary release, not proof that an effect occurred. The readback profile neither changes the closed core record nor introduces a sixth core state.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: The core protocol gates a downstream effect. This document binds that gate to HTTP without changing HTTP method semantics. The binding uses Structured Fields and Web Linking . These mechanisms do not themselves authenticate principals, enforce a deployment policy, or prove an external state change.

Three distinct conformance claims are defined: HTTP binding conformance, readback-profile conformance, and deployment conformance. A local simulator, a browser demonstration, or a successful build is not evidence that a remote executor conforms.

section.name: Conventions and Requirements
section.t: The capitalized requirement terms in this document have the meanings specified by BCP 14 . The core states remain EFFECT_NACK, EFFECT_ACK_CONTINUE, EFFECT_ACK_DONE, EFFECT_ACK_ISOLATE and EFFECT_ACK_BLOCK. Ordinary release requires a fresh, authenticated, independently validated core DONE record.

An action is the complete, immutable operation intended by the responsible principal. An execution is an attempt by an authorized executor. A readback is a distinct observation of the authoritative effect surface. An observer can be operated by the executor, but its identity, evidence sources and trust assumptions MUST be explicit; a separate request is not an assertion of institutional independence.

section.name: Capability Discovery
section.t: An origin supporting the HTTP binding SHOULD advertise an effect-ack link. Discovery is metadata, never authorization. A deployment MAY use a configured authenticated capability location. No well-known URI is allocated by this document.

The elected readback profile has the identifier eap-http-readback-1. Its capability representation is a separate JSON object, not the closed core capability object. It contains exactly the members http_profile, prepare_supported, commit_supported and readback_supported; their values MUST be eap-http-readback-1, true, true and true respectively. A client MUST authenticate the origin and validate the complete capability before sending a protected operation. A field that an unknown server may ignore MUST NOT be used as the sole protection against execution.

All network exchanges for this profile MUST use HTTPS with authenticated server identity and integrity protection. Client and observer authentication MUST follow the bound deployment policy. Cross-origin endpoints require an explicitly authorized destination and authentication context; redirects MUST NOT silently move protected requests or credentials to another authority.

section.name: Effect-Ack-Request Field
section.t: Effect-Ack-Request is a Structured Dictionary. Version 1 permits only v (Integer 1), mode (Token prepare or commit), token (Byte Sequence), and hash (Byte Sequence of 32 octets). Prepare contains exactly v and mode. Commit contains all four members. Duplicate dictionary keys, member parameters, unknown members, wrong types, malformed encodings and unsupported versions MUST prevent execution. An implementation MUST detect duplicate keys before a parser discards them.
section.sourcecode: Effect-Ack-Request: v=1, mode=prepare Effect-Ack-Request: v=1, mode=commit, token=:AQIDBAUGBwgJCgsMDQ4PEA==:, hash=:AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA=:
section.t: The second line is a syntax-only fixture, not a usable authorization. Production tokens MUST be unguessable, with at least 128 bits of entropy. A server receiving prepare MUST NOT execute the protected effect. Any reservation or other stateful preparation MUST itself be permitted by the applicable policy.

section.name: Effect-Ack Field and Record Hash
section.t: Effect-Ack is a Structured Dictionary with v (Integer 1), state (one of the Tokens nack, continue, done, isolate or block), hash (32-octet Byte Sequence), and optionally token (Byte Sequence). No other members or parameters are defined. A token MUST NOT be issued for a non-DONE record. The same parsing restrictions as for the request field apply.

The hash field identifies the complete responsibility record, including its core protocol_hash and created_utc members. After validation of the core normalization requirements, the complete object is serialized using JCS , and SHA-256 is applied to those UTF-8 octets. This full-record digest is distinct from the core protocol_hash, whose projection excludes specified members. Implementations MUST validate both digests under their respective definitions and MUST NOT substitute one for the other. Timestamp integrity does not by itself establish freshness.

The client obtains the full core record through the authenticated effect-ack link or an authenticated channel identified by the deployment policy. Compact fields cannot replace the core checks. A mismatch between compact state, full-record digest, rederived core state, or the expected action MUST prevent commit.

For the elected readback profile, a successful prepare response body is the prepare-envelope defined in . The full record is retrieved from record_uri. The action manifest is supplied in the envelope and its JCS SHA-256 identifier MUST occur in both evidence_refs and required_evidence_refs of the core record. Existing core fields are reused; unknown fields MUST NOT be added to the closed core record. A non-releasing prepare response has no commit token and need not contain a prepare-envelope.

section.name: Exact Action and Subject Binding
section.t: The action manifest binds the method, absolute effective target URI, request content, effect-relevant request metadata, responsible principal, executor, immutable source subject, policy, readback requirements and prerequisite receipts. The client MUST compare it with its own intended operation; accepting an executor-supplied manifest without this comparison is insufficient.

content_hash is SHA-256 of the HTTP message content octets in the sense used by Content-Digest , before decoding any content coding. The deployment policy MUST define a deterministic descriptor of all other effect-relevant request metadata, including content type and content coding when used. semantic_headers_hash binds that descriptor. Credentials and bearer tokens MUST NOT be included in a publicly retrievable manifest. The authenticated principal, not raw credential bytes, is bound. An undefined metadata comparison is a failure, not permission to ignore headers.

subject_hash identifies a separate immutable source-subject manifest. For a repository publication, it MUST identify repository authority, object-format-tagged full commit and tree identifiers, and every intended source artifact with byte length and SHA-256. A branch name, tag, title, current alias or predecessor tree alone is insufficient. That manifest MUST NOT contain its own digest or claim to bind a commit that includes its own newly generated receipt; action-time bindings are generated outside the immutable source checkout.

readback_requirements_hash identifies the exact requirements document: authorized observation authorities, permitted observer identities, resource selectors, expected postconditions, evidence formats, freshness/challenge rules and verifier implementation or procedure. Its bytes MUST be available and authenticated before commit. This document defines no universal interpreter for arbitrary business or physical postconditions. Two implementations lacking a common requirements document MUST NOT claim semantic interoperability.

preconditions contains sorted, unique receipt digests. Each required receipt MUST be authenticated and checked against the subject and relation required by that prerequisite. Array position, publication time and identifiers MUST NOT establish causal ordering. Missing, stale, failed, ambiguous or unbound prerequisites prevent execution.

section.name: Prepare and Commit Transaction

ol.li: Discover and authenticate support, freeze the intended request and action manifest, and verify all prerequisites.
Send the exact proposed HTTP operation with mode=prepare. Preparation does not execute the protected effect.
For a releasing result, obtain the full record and independently check the core algorithm, freshness, authenticated authority, all evidence bindings and exact action equivalence.

The server issues a short-lived, single-use token bound to the complete action hash, full-record hash, request equivalence, authenticated principal, executor and expiration. Expiration MUST be enforced by trusted executor state, not a client-supplied clock.

Repeat the exact operation with mode=commit, token and hash. The executor atomically revalidates these bindings, current authorization and prerequisites, and durably records token consumption before admitting execution.
Record an execution identifier and its immutable binding to operation_id, action hash, full-record hash and the token-consumption record. Expose the readback endpoint without disclosing the token.
Perform a distinct authoritative readback. Report confirmation only under . HTTP success, a queued job or a process exit code alone is insufficient.

section.t: Protected endpoints MUST reject effect-bearing requests that omit the required commit binding. All alternate paths to the same protected executor MUST enforce equivalent checks. A later revocation prevents future admissions; it does not retroactively undo an admitted or completed effect.

A change to request semantics, subject, policy, principal, executor, required evidence or readback requirements invalidates the prepared authorization. In repository workflows, any new commit identifier is a new validation subject even when its tree is unchanged. A new subject requires a new preparation and fresh applicable validation; predecessor receipts remain historical.

section.name: Replay, Crashes and Unknown Outcomes
section.t: The executor MUST durably deduplicate by authenticated principal, executor and operation_id, and MUST reject reuse of that tuple for a different action hash. A spent token MUST never admit a second execution. A repeated request MAY return a previously recorded status for the same operation, but MUST NOT repeat the protected effect.

Atomic token consumption is not a distributed exactly-once guarantee. A crash after consumption and before a reliable effect receipt can leave the outcome unknown. A timeout or lost response MUST be classified UNKNOWN, not as evidence that nothing happened. Automatic retransmission with a new token or operation identifier is prohibited while the outcome is unresolved. A distinct authenticated observation or an explicit authorized recovery plan is required.

Deployments MUST declare ledger durability, retention and recovery behavior. Spent-token records MUST be retained through the token validity and recovery horizon; operation deduplication records MUST cover the lifetime in which a client may retry that operation. Lost ledger state, exhaustion or unverifiable recovery MUST fail closed. Compensating an effect is a new separately authorized action, not erasure of the original receipt.

section.name: Authoritative Effect Readback
section.t: The readback_uri in the prepare-envelope MUST be an authenticated absolute HTTPS URI without a query or fragment. Its identity MUST be permitted by the bound readback requirements and remain associated with the execution. Following an execution attempt, the client generates a fresh 256-bit random challenge and sends GET to that URI with the query parameter challenge encoded as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Readback is observation-only and MUST NOT admit or retry a protected effect.

The authenticated observer obtains the authoritative source state, evaluates the bound requirements, and returns the closed readback object in using application/json. Responses MUST use Cache-Control: no-store. The observer MUST bind the challenge and all receipt fields through an authenticated integrity-protected channel or authenticated outer envelope. Merely reflecting the challenge around an old status is not a fresh observation.

For third-party platforms that do not implement this profile, an authorized observer MAY obtain a fresh authenticated platform read and attest to it. The receipt MUST identify the actual source and observer and preserve the source evidence bytes or their retrievable digests. An adapter's submission response, screenshot of its own local state, or unverifiable assertion is not an authoritative platform readback.

CONFIRMED is admissible only when the consumer validates the action and authorization bindings, execution identity, challenge, observer authority, source identity, resource version, all required evidence and the declared postconditions. resource_uri and resource_version MUST be non-null and evidence MUST be nonempty. The consumer MUST independently evaluate the conditions or validate the assertion of an observer explicitly authorized for that predicate. A wire value of CONFIRMED alone is not a valid confirmation.

REFUTED requires equally authoritative evidence that the required postcondition is false. UNKNOWN covers unavailable, stale, incomplete, ambiguous or unauthenticated evidence; the absence of a visible resource after a timeout does not automatically establish REFUTED. A malformed or untrusted receipt MUST NOT yield confirmation or authorize a retry.

A receipt sequence is an append-only observation chain for one execution. The first sequence is 1 with previous_receipt_hash null. A successor increments sequence by one and cites the JCS SHA-256 of the complete preceding receipt. A consumer MUST validate the chain and retain an authenticated anchor when rewrite detection is required. A hash chain alone proves neither authenticity nor causality. Subsequent observations can change the outcome; they do not rewrite historical observations.

The observation outcome is distinct from core authorization. This profile MUST NOT reinterpret EFFECT_ACK_DONE as an effect receipt. A downstream obligation requiring confirmation remains unsatisfied until a valid CONFIRMED receipt exists. A new downstream effect also requires its own core authorization.

section.name: Closed Readback-Profile Data Model
section.t: The following CDDL is normative for the auxiliary objects, not a replacement for core CDDL. JSON MUST be UTF-8 without a byte-order mark. Duplicate or unknown members, unsupported versions, floating-point values, non-finite numbers and invalid Unicode MUST be rejected. Auxiliary identifiers and URIs in this profile are printable ASCII; bounded-id is 1 through 256 characters and bounded-uri is 1 through 2048 characters. URI and HTTP-method validity are additional semantic checks. All SHA-256 identifiers have the indicated lowercase syntax. Arrays used as sets MUST be sorted and unique; no normalization or silent duplicate removal is permitted for these auxiliary objects. JCS applies to the complete object, with no omitted fields.
section.sourcecode: sha256-id = tstr .regexp "^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$" challenge-id = tstr .regexp "^[0-9a-f]{64}$" bounded-id = tstr bounded-uri = tstr positive-int = 1..9007199254740991 receipt-set = [*128 sha256-id] http-capability = { http_profile: "eap-http-readback-1", prepare_supported: true, commit_supported: true, readback_supported: true } action-manifest = { profile: "eap-http-readback-1", operation_id: bounded-id, subject_hash: sha256-id, method: bounded-id, target: bounded-uri, content_hash: sha256-id, semantic_headers_hash: sha256-id, policy_hash: sha256-id, responsible_principal: bounded-id, executor: bounded-uri, readback_requirements_hash: sha256-id, preconditions: receipt-set } prepare-envelope = { http_profile: "eap-http-readback-1", record_uri: bounded-uri, action: action-manifest, readback_uri: bounded-uri } readback = { profile: "eap-http-readback-1", action_hash: sha256-id, authorization_record_hash: sha256-id, execution_id: bounded-id, challenge: challenge-id, observer: bounded-id, source_uri: bounded-uri, resource_uri: bounded-uri / null, resource_version: bounded-id / null, outcome: "CONFIRMED" / "REFUTED" / "UNKNOWN", evidence: receipt-set, sequence: positive-int, previous_receipt_hash: sha256-id / null }
section.t: Consumers MUST enforce bounded message size before parsing; a deployment MUST specify its limit and MUST reject oversized objects without executing an effect. An implementation advertising this profile MUST accept auxiliary objects up to 65536 octets and MAY impose that limit. Evidence bodies are external, digest-addressed objects with separate deployment limits; inlining unbounded evidence is not permitted.

section.name: Backward Compatibility
section.t: The base HTTP binding remains opt-in. A legacy recipient may ignore unfamiliar HTTP fields, so a fail-closed client MUST establish support before sending protected operations. A client requiring eap-http-readback-1 MUST NOT silently downgrade to preparation-only, core-only, or transport-only support. The core version-1 schema, five outcomes, DONE predicate and protocol_hash definition remain unchanged.

The readback profile is external evidence carried beside core records. Older implementations lacking this profile are not thereby invalid core implementations; they simply cannot satisfy an obligation requiring the stronger profile.

section.name: HTML Integration
section.t: An ordinary HTML link element can advertise the proposed effect-ack relation. No new element, parser feature or browser permission is defined. Link presence is discovery only. Browser user interfaces MUST distinguish local preview, submitted input, prepared authorization, execution attempt, unknown outcome and authoritative confirmation.

section.name: Browser Proxy Considerations
section.t: A proxy MUST preserve source identity and all exact-action bindings. Audio, video and screen capture require explicit user permission and submission; local preview is not an instruction to transmit. Browser permissions and session possession are not effect authorization. A proxy MUST NOT manufacture a native review, signature, publication status or remote effect receipt from a rendered page or a local return value.

Runtime confirmation for a remote terminal requires the declared runtime observation, not just an OCI build or deployment request. A profile can require exact image and source digests, a running browser process and an observable interactive surface. It MUST identify which of those facts were actually observed; a simulation is not physical hardware execution.

section.name: Intermediaries, Caches and CORS
section.t: Intermediaries MUST NOT synthesize authorization or confirmation. Any transformation of bound request content or effect-relevant metadata invalidates the preparation unless that transformation is explicitly included in the action and independently validated. Protected commit endpoints MUST NOT rely on cache state to prevent replay.

Tokens, prepared authorizations and readbacks MUST use Cache-Control: no-store. Script access remains subject to ordinary CORS and Fetch rules. Cross-origin credential delegation requires explicit policy; an advertised link does not grant it.

section.name: Conformance and Validation Boundaries
section.t: HTTP binding tests MUST cover syntax rejection, unknown versions, request substitution, non-DONE rejection, expiration, replay, policy change and alternate-path protection. Readback tests MUST additionally reject stale challenges, action or subject changes, mismatched authorization and execution identities, untrusted observers, missing evidence, unsupported resource versions and false confirmation after timeout.

A reference predicate over synthetic already-verified inputs tests only the decision relation. It does not implement authentication, an HTTP parser, durable distributed execution, a native review authority, a browser runtime, or empirical validation. Conformance claims MUST list the executed test scope and exact implementation subject; source inspection and workflow transport cannot substitute for execution evidence.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: Threats include forged DONE or CONFIRMED values, token theft, replay, stale-record substitution, confused deputies, SSRF through evidence links, parser differentials, duplicate members, ledger rollback, mutable resource aliases and compromised observers. A content digest proves integrity only relative to a trusted digest. Authentication and authority for a specific predicate remain separate checks.

Implementations MUST restrict evidence retrieval to policy-authorized schemes and authorities, bound sizes and redirects, and avoid forwarding credentials to arbitrary references. HTTP Message Signatures MAY authenticate selected HTTP components under an explicit deployment profile; their mere presence does not make a receipt trustworthy. TLS endpoint authentication does not establish that a claimed physical effect occurred.

section.name: Privacy Considerations
section.t: Subject manifests, principals and evidence references can expose sensitive activity. Deployments MUST apply appropriate access controls, minimize public metadata, and keep credentials out of source and public receipts. Retention and erasure policies MUST distinguish durable deduplication state from optional personal evidence; erasure cannot silently restore an operation's execution eligibility.

section.name: HTTP Field Name Registration Requests
section.t: This document requests provisional HTTP Field Name Registry entries for Effect-Ack and Effect-Ack-Request, both Structured Dictionaries, with references to and respectively. These are requests, not assertions that registrations have occurred.

section.name: Link Relation Registration Request
section.t: This document requests the relation name effect-ack: identifies an endpoint or representation for EFFECT_ACK capability information or the responsibility record bound to the link context. The reference is this document. No well-known URI, media type, new core state or new core field is requested.

front.title: QIK-VRT Effect Acknowledgement: Separating Receipt from Authorization for Downstream Effect

section.name: Repository Publication Profile
section.t: This appendix is an application profile, not a change to the general core protocol. The QIK-VRT repository requires an explicit causal chain: manifest latest knowledge; build one integration head; validate that exact head; obtain required review on that same validated head; freshly reobserve the unchanged head after review; legitimately promote; freshly observe the resulting exact Main; derive exact-Main-bound external obligations. Any head mutation resets candidate validation and downstream bindings. The source manifest and effect receipts are separate to avoid self-referential commit hashing.

Wikipedia, Zenodo, arXiv and IETF effects are independent only when their explicitly declared common prerequisite is satisfied. Deferral of one destination is not completion of that destination. A GitHub automated comment is not native Code-Owner approval; a merge is not publication on another platform.

An IETF submission receipt binds the exact draft name, revision, submitted XML bytes and submission identifier. Public draft appearance requires a separate Datatracker readback. The source XML and service-generated TXT/HTML are distinct artifacts: differences introduced by an identified platform renderer must be reported and reviewed rather than asserted byte-identical. A document's existence does not establish IETF consensus, working-group adoption, RFC publication or standards status.

Zenodo confirmation requires the authoritative record, DOI and exact public fileset; arXiv submission and later public-version status are separate milestones; Wikipedia request creation and acceptance are separate milestones. None establishes empirical confirmation of a scientific claim. A local-change-time provenance profile can supply source-order evidence, but does not authorize an effect or establish physical retrocausality.

section.name: Candidate Status
section.t: This repository candidate is prepared for author review and deterministic rendering. It is not evidence of a Datatracker upload. Before submission, the actual current document name and revision, final source bytes, author account, applicable submission terms, exact source subject and authorization must be bound and reobserved. Historical source and receipts are retained; no predecessor validation is transferred.
